This diagnosis is supported by the early onset of bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance. The “double bubble” sign on abdominal X-ray — representing air-filled stomach and proximal duodenum with no distal gas — is pathognomonic for duodenal atresia. This finding, combined with the neonatal onset and absence of distal bowel gas, strongly excludes other causes of high obstruction (e.g., malrotation with midgut volvulus, which typically shows diffuse distension and may have a “corkscrew” or “whirlpool” sign on imaging, not isolated double bubble).
